sentences.text:
The offences alleged against the petitioner is under Sections 376 and 384 of IPC.
2.

The prosecution case is that the petitioner, after promising to marry the de facto complainant,
sexually abused her during the period from July 2017 till 17.09.2017 and thereby, he is alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.
3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the entire disputes between the petitioner and the de facto complainant were settled.
Therefore she prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
4. The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent/de facto complainant also submitted that the entire disputes between the petitioner and the de facto complainant were settled.
Therefore, he also prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
5. The petition was opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor.

6. On a perusal of the FI statement itself, it is revealed that the de facto complainant was already married to another person, and it was at that time, she started living along with the petitioner under the alleged promise of marriage.
Therefore, from the FI statement, it is revealed that the relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant was a consensual one.

Her claim that she had given consent to the petitioner, because of the promise of marriage cannot be believed as she was already married to another person and the said marriage was till subsisting, when she maintained the relationship with the petitioner.
Further, the entire disputes between the parties were already settled.
7. In the above circumstances, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings against the petitioner, as the same will only be an abuse of the process of Court.
In the result, this Crl. M.C is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioner in L.P.No.14 of 2023 of 2026:KER:488 Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Chengannur, arising from Crime No.1464 of 2017 of Mannar Police Station, is quashed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
